## Formula syntax conflict behavior

These examples define precedence where GitHub formula compatibility and LaTeX
compatibility touch existing Markdown syntax or each other.

Code spans bind before formula delimiters inside the span.

```````````````````````````````` example
Code `$x$` and formula $x$.
.
Document scope=1:1..1:27 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:27 anchor=null attributes={} children=5
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} literal="Code " children=0
    ├── Code scope=1:6..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} literal="$x$" children=0
    ├── Text scope=1:11..1:23 anchor=null attributes={} literal=" and formula " children=0
    ├── Formula scope=1:24..1:26 anchor=null attributes={} mode=embedded literal="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:27..1:27 anchor=null attributes={} literal="." children=0
````````````````````````````````

The GitHub `$`...`$` formula form binds as formula, not as a code span.

```````````````````````````````` example
Formula $`x`$ not code.
.
Document scope=1:1..1:23 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:23 anchor=null attributes={} children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} literal="Formula " children=0
    ├── Formula scope=1:9..1:13 anchor=null attributes={} mode=embedded literal="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:14..1:23 anchor=null attributes={} literal=" not code." children=0
````````````````````````````````

A same-line display close followed by non-whitespace trailing text is inline
display formula inside a paragraph, not a formula block.

```````````````````````````````` example
$$x$$ trailing
.
Document scope=1:1..1:14 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:14 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Formula scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} mode=standalone literal="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:6..1:14 anchor=null attributes={} literal=" trailing" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
\\[x\\] trailing
.
Document scope=1:1..1:16 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:16 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Formula scope=1:1..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} mode=standalone literal="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:8..1:16 anchor=null attributes={} literal=" trailing" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Indented code takes precedence over formula block openers.

```````````````````````````````` example
    $$x$$
.
Document scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── CodeBlock scope=1:5..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} info=null language=null literal="$$x$$\n" fenced=false closed=true children=0
````````````````````````````````

Non-`formula` fenced code remains ordinary code.

```````````````````````````````` example
```js
$x$
```
.
Document scope=1:1..3:3 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── CodeBlock scope=1:1..3:3 anchor=null attributes={} info="js" language="js" literal="$x$\n" fenced=true closed=true children=0
````````````````````````````````

A backslash closer with nothing to close is not a formula delimiter. The base
language keeps its escaped backslash, so a bracket that follows one still
closes a reference (CommonMark 0.31.2 example 558).

```````````````````````````````` example
[bar\\]: /uri

[bar\\] and \\) alone.
.
Document scope=1:1..3:22 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=3:1..3:22 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Link scope=3:1..3:7 anchor=null attributes={} dest=url("/uri") title=null children=1
    │   └── Text scope=3:2..3:6 anchor=null attributes={} literal="bar\\" children=0
    └── Text scope=3:8..3:22 anchor=null attributes={} literal=" and \\) alone." children=0
````````````````````````````````

One formula of a form is open at a time: an opener inside an open body of its
own form is the body's bytes, and the first closer of the form ends the body.
The trailing `\\)` then has nothing to close and is the base language's
escaped backslash and a parenthesis.

```````````````````````````````` example
\\(a \\(b\\) c\\)
.
Document scope=1:1..1:17 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:17 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Formula scope=1:1..1:12 anchor=null attributes={} mode=embedded literal="a \\\\(b" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:13..1:17 anchor=null attributes={} literal=" c\\)" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A closer whose opener an earlier closer already took is the same case.

```````````````````````````````` example
\\(x\\) and \\) again.
.
Document scope=1:1..1:22 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:22 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Formula scope=1:1..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} mode=embedded literal="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:8..1:22 anchor=null attributes={} literal=" and \\) again." children=0
````````````````````````````````

Code spans also bind before LaTeX backslash delimiters.

```````````````````````````````` example
Code `\\(x\\)` and formula \\(x\\).
.
Document scope=1:1..1:35 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:35 anchor=null attributes={} children=5
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} literal="Code " children=0
    ├── Code scope=1:6..1:14 anchor=null attributes={} literal="\\\\(x\\\\)" children=0
    ├── Text scope=1:15..1:27 anchor=null attributes={} literal=" and formula " children=0
    ├── Formula scope=1:28..1:34 anchor=null attributes={} mode=embedded literal="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:35..1:35 anchor=null attributes={} literal="." children=0
````````````````````````````````
